deities: Maya Devi (three-headed, four-armed Shakti; Adhishtatri deity of Haridwar)

history.dynasty: Not established (ancient shrine, no documented builder)
history.summary: Maya Devi Temple near Birla Ghat is one of Haridwar's oldest shrines and one of only three ancient Haridwar temples still standing intact (with the Narayana-shila and Bhairava temples). It is a Shakti Peeth: tradition holds that the heart and navel of Goddess Sati fell here, and it is one of the three Siddh Peeths of Haridwar (with Mansa Devi and Chandi Devi). Maya Devi, the Adhishtatri (guardian deity) of Haridwar, is depicted as a three-headed, four-armed goddess; the sanctum houses Maya in the centre with Kali on the left and Kamakhya on the right. The ancient city was called Mayapuri (Mayapur) in her honour. The pradakshina path around the sanctum bears illustrations of the Dasha Mahavidyas, and the complex also contains the Narayana-shila and Anand Bhairav temples, managed by the Juna Akhara, which offers free meals morning and evening.

name: Maya Devi Temple
town_description: Haridwar, in the Haridwar district of Uttarakhand at the foothills of the Sivalik Hills where the Ganga enters the plains, is one of Hinduism's seven holy cities (Sapta Puri) and one of the four Kumbh Mela sites. Its spiritual heart is Har Ki Pauri, where the evening Ganga Aarti draws thousands daily. Mansa Devi and Chandi Devi temples crown the twin hills (Bilwa Parvat and Neel Parvat) overlooking the city, while the Maya Devi temple sits near Birla Ghat and Daksheshwar Mahadev lies in the adjoining heritage township of Kankhal.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approx. 35-40 km; taxis and pre-paid cabs available).
travel.railway: Haridwar Junction (approx. 600 m; walk or auto-rickshaw to the temple at Upper Road / Birla Ghat).
travel.road: Easily reached by auto-rickshaws and city buses from Har Ki Pauri; well connected by road to Delhi, Rishikesh and Dehradun via NH-58.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, and Navratri and Kumbh Mela are the most vibrant (and crowded) periods. Avoid Shravan (Kanwar Yatra) for casual sightseeing. Mornings 6:30-9:00 AM are best for quiet darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opening hours conflict across sources (verify): commonly 6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00-8:00 PM, or 6:30 AM-12:00 PM and 3:00-9:00 PM. Morning and evening aartis daily. No entry fee.
